title: Multiplying by 10 with place value blocks
examples: What happens when you multiply by 10?
Why do we add a zero when multiplying by 10?

explain.say: One box holds 23 crayons. How many crayons are in 10 boxes? Let us see what times 10 does. Look at the board: 23 is 2 tens and 3 ones.

draw.text: Multiplying by 10 with place value blocks

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: base-ten blocks. Can you see the thousand and the hundreds? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Multiplying by 10 with place value blocks

explain.say: Start with the 3 ones. Ten lots of 3 ones make 30, so each one grows into a ten. See the 3 rods? Every little cube became a rod!
Now the 2 tens. Ten lots of a ten make a hundred, so each rod grows into a flat. 2 tens become 2 hundreds, which is 200. Can you guess the whole answer?
Put it together: 200 and 30 make 230. So 23 times 10 is 230. Every digit moved one place to the left, and a zero holds the empty ones place. Can you see the zero doing its job?
Amazing! So 45 times 10 is 450: the 4 moves to the hundreds and the 5 to the tens. Wow: our number system is built on tens, so this trick works for any number. What is 67 times 10?

faq.q: What happens when you multiply by 10?
faq.a: Every digit moves one place to the left and becomes 10 times bigger. Ones become tens, and tens become hundreds. A zero fills the empty ones place.
asks: Why do digits move when I times by 10?

faq.a: 23 times 10 is 230. The 2 tens become 2 hundreds, and the 3 ones become 3 tens.

faq.q: Why do we add a zero when multiplying by 10?
faq.a: The zero is not really added on. The digits move one place left, the ones place is left empty, and we put a zero there to hold the place.
Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left. 23 times 100 is 2,300.

faq.q: Does this work for every number?
faq.a: Yes. Our number system is based on tens, so multiplying by 10 always moves each digit one place to the left.
asks: Does times 10 always work like this?

facts: Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place to the left.

quiz.why: 5 tens become 5 hundreds and 6 ones become 6 tens: 560.

wrong.0: 5610 just sticks 10 on the end instead of moving the digits.
wrong.1: 506 puts the zero in the wrong place.

quiz.say: When you multiply 34 by 10, what is the 3 worth?
quiz.show: When you multiply 34 by 10, what is the 3 worth?
quiz.why: The 3 was 3 tens; it moves one place left to be 3 hundreds, 300.

wrong.1: 30 is what the 3 was worth before multiplying.
wrong.2: 3 would be a 3 in the ones place.
